summary: First iteration of ZapingX IPTV clone tested end-to-end. Backend: 22/22 pytest cases pass after a small fix (invalid credentials now return 401 instead of 500). All required endpoints work against real Xtream server (auth, live categories/channels/play with hidden URL, VOD categories/streams/info, series categories/list/info with per-episode URLs) and all authenticated endpoints reject requests without an Authorization header. Frontend: Login → tabs navigation works; Home hero + 3 rows (Live/Movies/Series) render; Live tab shows 224 channels with working search; Movies shows real posters and reports 29,769 titles; Series tab loads; Profile shows correct username 1q1q1q1q and Logout returns to Login. No deprecated Expo packages (expo-video used instead of expo-av). No SafeAreaView misuse. No React Native red screens.
action_items: None blocking. Optional: verify live video playback on a native build (expo-video on web may not play some HLS/UA-gated streams — expected per E1 note).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py login() did not wrap the JSON parse from Xtream, so invalid credentials caused a 500 due to JSONDecodeError. Fixed by catching JSONDecodeError/ValueError and non-dict responses → returning 401.
In-memory M3U cache (30 min TTL) is fine for single-instance deployment; will need shared cache if scaled horizontally.
verify=False on the Xtream httpx client disables TLS validation — acceptable because the provider uses a self-signed cert, but worth documenting.
seed_data_creation: None. Live data comes from Xtream/M3U.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Frontend uses EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL (not EXPO_BACKEND_URL) in /app/frontend/.env. Xtream credentials in /app/memory/test_credentials.md (1q1q1q1q/1q1q1q1q). Base test file: /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py. React Native TextInput on web preview must be filled with keyboard.type() after clicking – fill() does not update state.
rca_of_issue: Invalid-credentials 500: Xtream returns a non-JSON response body (empty/HTML) when auth fails; httpx r.json() raised JSONDecodeError which propagated as 500. Root cause: login() only caught httpx.HTTPError, missing JSON decode error path. Mitigation applied: catch JSONDecodeError/ValueError and non-dict payloads and return 401 with the standard message.
